# Why Varuṇa is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *varuna*. This is the file on how **Varuṇa** replaced it.

Varuṇa is the Vedic sovereign of the cosmic order (ṛta), the lord of waters, and the guardian of truth. He binds offenders with his noose (pāśa), sends a thousand spies to watch the world, and holds the night sky in his sway. To swear falsely before Varuṇa is to invite disease, disaster, and cosmic rupture. Varuṇa is praised in the Ṛgveda as the god who sees all and knows all.  His spies — the thousand-eyed — move through the world observing every act, every lie, every hidden crime.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Varuṇa
- **ASCII form:** varuna
- **Meaning:** "The All-Enveloping Sky — the Vedic Āditya of the waters and of ṛta, paired with Mitra"
- **Domain of influence:** Cosmic Order, Oceans, Law
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** वरुण
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 258 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Varuṇa** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *varuna* and **Varuṇa** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Varuṇa** lives at [/sites/varuna/](/sites/varuna/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/varuna/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/varuna/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/varuna/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Varuṇa** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Freshwater & Hydrology** — Lord of all waters — rivers, seas, rain, and the underworld streams; the Vedic sovereign of the whole supply.
- **Legal, Justice & Compliance** — The order that binds; law as cosmic covenant.
- **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** — Lord of the oceans and the order that governs them.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
